# pidginhost_ipv6 (Resource)

Allocates a public IPv6 address. Attach it to a server with `pidginhost_ipv6_attachment`, or pass it to a new server as `public_ipv6`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_ipv6" "mail" {
  reverse_dns = "mail.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `reverse_dns` (String) Reverse DNS (PTR) name, for example `host.example.com`. Can be changed in place. When omitted, the API's default is kept. The API cannot remove a PTR record, so removing this argument leaves the current name in place.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) The allocated address.
- `attached` (Boolean) Whether the address is attached to a server.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway for the address.
- `id` (String) Address ID.
- `prefix` (Number) Prefix length of the address's network.
- `server_id` (String) ID of the server the address is attached to, or null.
- `slug` (String) Slug of the address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an IPv6 address by its ID.
terraform import pidginhost_ipv6.mail 123
```
